topic.title: Is getting a gold mandatory for becoming a finalist in the strategy competition?

messages.content: at least you need to show proof that those criteria in the strategy track rubrics are met. E.g. My agent can learn strategy … how it is shown? local cv and simulation track. Your agent will be run against others after the deadline for about 2 weeks and this will verify if your claims is correct

replies.content: Your example reminded me of a question I've been wondering about. Initially when I read the rubrics, I interpreted a higher emphasis on an adaptable AI agent (i.e. an agent that can be given any deck and it would know how to play it based on its learning), if that is even possible. Although, I'm working with the different assumption that I just need to teach the agent the strategy it will be using with its fixed deck (and improving that strategy), I can't help but wonder if I'm digging my own grave.

replies.content:
Imagine 2 strategy track submission

  1. Claim to be very adaptable etc and prove on addition local experiments and public lb rank 10% and public notebook. But rank 50% on private rank
  2. Claim is not as good as 1. But local cv and public/private rank are consistent at 25%

messages.content: I believe these are always particular to the competition hosts (what they value). I haven't been on Kaggle long, but my personal take so far is that these are largely "exclude from the top" clauses more so than "include from the bottom."

messages.content: The LB performance for this competition is taken into account for the strategy competition. I have not participated in competitions like this before. So can silver/bronze/non medalists hope to be a finalist in the strategy competition? Is it often determined solely by the LB (the best models in the LB could be interpreted to have the best strategy)?
